ball.a: Ice hockey, as a goalkeeper for Dynamo Moscow

ball.q: One man has played in two World Cup finals for two different countries. Who?
ball.a: Luis Monti, for Argentina in 1930 and Italy in 1934

ball.q: At Corinthians in the early 1980s, Sócrates and his teammates ran the club by vote. What were they voting on?
ball.a: Everything, from the team selection to wages and travel, one man one vote including the kit man

ball.q: Ruud Gullit won the Ballon d'Or in 1987 and dedicated it to a man in prison. Who?
English referee Andy Wain abandoned a Sunday league match in 2005 after squaring up to a goalkeeper. What had he done first?
ball.a: Sent himself off, saying he would have sent off any player who did that

ball.q: Colombian midfielder Gerardo Bedoya holds a Guinness record for the wrong reasons. What is it?
ball.a: Most red cards in a professional career, 46

ball.q: A Seville derby in the 2007 Copa del Rey was abandoned and finished behind closed doors in Getafe. Why?
ball.a: Sevilla coach Juande Ramos was knocked unconscious by a bottle thrown from the stand

ball.q: Atlético Madrid were nearly bankrupt after the Spanish Civil War and merged with another club to survive. Who with?
ball.a: Aviación Nacional, the air force club, making them Atlético Aviación

ball.q: Spanish goalkeeper Ricardo Zamora was reported shot dead in 1936, then found alive in a Madrid prison. What is said to have kept him there?
ball.a: Playing football with the guards, until the Argentine embassy got him out

ball.q: When Athletic Bilbao win a major trophy they parade it in a way no other club does. How?
ball.a: On a barge, the gabarra, down the river Nervión into Bilbao

ball.q: Barcelona's motto més que un club was not invented by a marketing department. Who said it first, in 1968?
ball.a: Club president Narcís de Carreras, in his nomination speech

ball.q: After Cruyff's Barcelona won 5-0 at the Bernabéu in February 1974, what did Catalans keep saying to him instead of congratulations?
Roger Milla was retired and playing on Réunion when he was talked back into the Cameroon squad for the 1990 World Cup. Who talked him round?
ball.a: Paul Biya, the president of Cameroon, who phoned him

ball.q: Brian Clough bought a striker from Long Eaton United for 2,000 pounds and won two European Cups with him. What was the player's day job before that?
ball.a: Carpet fitter, he was Garry Birtles

ball.q: Which club won 6-3 at Ajax's De Meer stadium in April 1980?
In 1973 Chile kicked off a World Cup play-off in an empty stadium, walked the ball into the net and the referee ended it. Where was the other team?
ball.a: The Soviet Union refused to play in a stadium Pinochet had used as a prison

ball.q: Iceland's thunderclap looks ancient but is not. Where did their fans pick it up?
ball.a: From Motherwell fans, when Stjarnan played at Fir Park in 2014

ball.q: Ajax's founders named the club after a Greek warrior for one specific reason. What was it?
ball.a: Ajax killed himself rather than be beaten, so he died unconquered

ball.q: Sparta Rotterdam's red and white stripes came from a board trip to England in 1899. Which club's kit did they copy?
Faas Wilkes was banned from the Dutch national team from 1949 to 1955 in his prime. What had he done wrong?
ball.a: Turned professional abroad, which the amateur-only KNVB would not allow

ball.q: On the last day of the 1999 season, Carlisle United needed a goal in the final seconds to stay in the Football League. Who scored it?
ball.a: Their on-loan goalkeeper Jimmy Glass, who had come up for a corner
